heading.en: Accession and the new era name

body.zh-Hant: 宮內廳陵墓資料記明治天皇為第122代天皇，父為孝明天皇，母為中山慶子。宮內廳年表載，睦仁親王於慶應3年（1867）1月9日踐祚，同年12月9日下王政復古的御沙汰；明治元年（1868）3月14日頒布五箇條御誓文，8月27日行即位禮，9月8日改慶應4年為明治。年表記日本至明治5年12月3日才改用太陽曆，以該日為明治6年1月1日，上述月日均在改曆之前（舊曆）。
body.en: The Imperial Household Agency lists Emperor Meiji as the 122nd emperor, with Emperor Komei as his father and Nakayama Yoshiko as his mother. Its chronology records that Prince Mutsuhito acceded on the 9th day of the 1st month of Keio 3 (1867) and that the restoration of imperial rule was announced on the 9th day of the 12th month that year; in Meiji 1 (1868) the Charter Oath followed on 3/14, the enthronement ceremony on 8/27, and on 9/8 the era was changed from Keio 4 to Meiji. The chronology notes that Japan adopted the solar calendar only from Meiji 5/12/3, which became 1 January Meiji 6, so these month-day dates are in the old calendar.

heading.en: Institution building and the imperial family

body.zh-Hant: 宮內廳年表記載：明治4年（1871）7月14日（舊曆）廢藩置縣；1889年2月11日頒布大日本帝國憲法，並裁定皇室典範。1900年5月10日皇太子嘉仁親王與九條節子結婚，1901年4月29日裕仁親王（後來的昭和天皇）誕生。
body.en: The Imperial Household Agency chronology records the abolition of the domains and creation of prefectures on the 14th day of the 7th month of Meiji 4 (1871, old calendar) and, on 11 February 1889, the promulgation of the Constitution of the Empire of Japan together with the Imperial House Law. Crown Prince Yoshihito married Kujo Sadako on 10 May 1900, and Prince Hirohito, later the Showa Emperor, was born on 29 April 1901.

body.zh-Hant: 宮內廳年表記載：1908年1月1日宮內省官制施行；1909年2月11日制定登極令、攝政令等；1910年8月29日發布韓國併合的詔書。1912年7月30日明治天皇崩御，皇太子嘉仁親王踐祚，改元大正。
body.en: The Imperial Household Agency chronology records the entry into force of the Imperial Household Ministry regulations on 1 January 1908 and, on 11 February 1909, the enactment of the Accession Ordinance and the Regency Ordinance among others. The rescript on the annexation of Korea was issued on 29 August 1910. Emperor Meiji died on 30 July 1912; Crown Prince Yoshihito acceded and the era was renamed Taisho.

people.name: Eleftherios Venizelos
people.nameZh: 埃萊夫塞里奧斯·韋尼澤洛斯

body.zh-Hant: 韋尼澤洛斯1864年8月23日生於奧斯曼統治下的克里特，在雅典大學修法律，是克里特與希臘統一運動的領導人之一。1899至1901年他任克里特司法大臣。1908年10月克里特人宣布與希臘合併，他是希臘政府所派委員會中最突出的人物。
body.en: Venizelos was born on 23 August 1864 in Ottoman-ruled Crete, studied law at the University of Athens, and became one of the leaders of the movement for the union of Crete with Greece. He served as Cretan minister of justice from 1899 to 1901. In October 1908 the Cretans proclaimed union with Greece, and he stood out as the strong man of the committee appointed by the Greek government.

body.zh-Hant: 1909年8月雅典發生軍事政變，軍人聯盟請他來希臘領導改革。他1910年1月抵達雅典，同年10月出任首相，並成立自由黨；1912年大選大勝，希臘打了1912至1913年兩次巴爾幹戰爭。第一次世界大戰爆發時，國王康斯坦丁不讓希臘站到協約國一方，他在1915年去職。
body.en: A military revolt broke out in Athens in August 1909 and the Military League asked Venizelos to come to Greece to lead reform. He arrived in Athens in January 1910, became prime minister in October 1910 and founded the Liberal Party; after a sweeping victory in the 1912 election, Greece fought the two Balkan Wars of 1912 to 1913. When the First World War broke out King Constantine blocked Greece from joining the Entente, and Venizelos had to step down in 1915.

heading.en: The Salonica government and electoral defeat

body.zh-Hant: 1916年8月，他因與主張中立的國王康斯坦丁對立，在薩洛尼卡另立對立政府。他再度出任首相，希臘加入協約國作戰。1920年11月選舉失敗，他數日後離開希臘。
body.en: In August 1916, after his dispute with the neutralist King Constantine, he set up a rival government in Salonica. He became prime minister again, and Greece entered the war on the side of the Entente. He lost the election of November 1920 and left the country a few days later.

heading.zh-Hant: 洛桑、第二段任期與逝世
heading.en: Lausanne, the second premiership and death

body.zh-Hant: 1923年7月24日簽署洛桑條約時，他是希臘代表團團長。他1928年再度出任首相；1930年6月10日與土耳其達成協議，同年10月30日簽友好條約。他1932年選舉落敗，1936年3月18日在巴黎逝世。
body.en: He headed the Greek delegation that signed the Treaty of Lausanne on 24 July 1923. He became prime minister again in 1928; an agreement with Turkey settling outstanding disputes followed on 10 June 1930 and a pact of friendship on 30 October 1930. He lost the 1932 election and died in Paris on 18 March 1936.

heading.en: Origins and leadership of the Civilista Party

body.zh-Hant: 帕爾多生於1864年，父親曼努埃爾·帕爾多是秘魯第一位任滿的文人總統。1904年卡內多在任內猝逝，帕爾多繼承了文人黨的領導地位。
body.en: Pardo was born in 1864, the son of Manuel Pardo y Lavalle, Peru's first full-term civilian president. When Manuel Candamo died suddenly in office in 1904, Pardo inherited the leadership of the Civilista Party.

body.zh-Hant: 帕爾多第一次出任秘魯總統是1904至1908年。這四年間，他把學校經費提高250%，並延伸主要鐵路。
body.en: Pardo's first term as president of Peru ran from 1904 to 1908. Over those four years he raised school spending by 250 percent and extended the main railway lines.

heading.en: The second term and the general strike

body.zh-Hant: 1915至1919年他第二度出任總統；當時在軍方促請下，文人黨、自由黨與憲政黨支持同一位候選人。1919年1月1日秘魯發生史上第一次總罷工，工人與大學生聯合要求普遍實行八小時工作制。
body.en: He served a second term as president from 1915 to 1919, when, at military urging, the Civilista, Liberal and Constitutionalist parties backed a common candidate. On 1 January 1919 Peru saw its first general strike, in which workers and university students together demanded a universal eight-hour working day.

doctor en Ciencias Políticas y Administrativas y se graduó de abogado (1896)
Manuel Candamo ganó las elecciones de 1903
lo nombró ministro de Relaciones Exteriores
Candamo falleció al poco tiempo
Serapio Calderón, el segundo vicepresidente
quien enseguida convocó a elecciones
representando al Partido Civil, ganó la confrontación electoral
Al ceñirse la banda presidencial, el 24 de setiembre de 1904
Pardo tenía 40 años
la educación primaria devino en obligatoria y gratuita en toda la República
se fundó la Escuela Nacional de Varones para la formación de docentes
logró solucionar los conflictos fronterizos con Ecuador
mediante la firma de un tratado
potenció la Marina con los cruceros Grau y Bolognesi
viajó a Europa, donde residió seis años
fue elegido rector de la Universidad de San Marcos
cargo que declinó al verse ungido nuevamente presidente de la República
promovió un golpe de Estado antes de que finalizara el gobierno de Pardo
Este fue encerrado en el Panóptico y, luego de ocho días, deportado
Su exilio lo pasó en Biarritz, Francia, donde permaneció 25 años
En 1944, reclamado por un importante movimiento de opinión, regresó al país
el 3 de agosto de 1947, falleció en el distrito de Miraflores
